object_description: new hall paired with the school building, its main volume flanked by single-storey annexes under long canopies
geometry_property: main hall volume with single-storey annexes on both long sides
generous canopies over the full length
visible timber frame with glass infill
design_condition: the new hall and the school form a pair set back from the street to create an address, while the social building closes the grounds to the east and turns towards the church

positive: Together with the school building the new construction forms a pair set back from the street, forming an address
The new hall blends naturally into its surroundings, creating a sense of identity
It gives the newly created ensemble an appealing appearance
The expression is friendly and inviting and conveys a lightness contrasting with the existing school
The visible timber frame construction filled with wooden elements and glass matches the room layout
A generous canopy over the full length welcomes visitors on the north side
The southern canopy similarly welcomes pupils from the school grounds
The building is entered from the public forecourt via a square foyer at hall level
A second elongated foyer forms a generously dimensioned and versatile pre-zone
The equipment room on the opposite side of the hall is conveniently located
The checkroom wing under the stage is an interesting solution accessible from both entrances
The stage area with flanking multi-purpose rooms is raised and individually accessible via the forestage
The stage areas open onto the schoolyard, allowing the outdoor space to be used from the stage
The organisation and distribution of functions is coherent and ensures short distances
Several access points give a high degree of permeability and create links to the surroundings
The project is very efficient and in the lower third of the compared projects in dimensions
The clearly structured design leads to relatively low construction costs
Building structure and organisation are precise and coherent with an appealing architectural interpretation
A convincing contribution with a high level of functionality and great benefits for population and school
negative: The spatial proximity to the school building is borderline and the distance could have been better balanced
The decoupling of the social building is neither operationally nor spatially convincing
By position, orientation and geometry it appears to belong to the church and contributes little to the school grounds
The external venetian blinds are not wind-resistant, which can lead to overheating
Whether the shading measures will impair the desired transparent appearance is questionable
The transparent partition between foyer and hall causes mutual interference for evening events
Direct access from the underground garage for evening sports is not planned
The underground car park is clearly but inefficiently organised
Rear access to the stage is only possible via the lift
The ramp and bicycle shelter appear bulky and cut through the generous open space
Not preserving the existing copper beech is incomprehensible
The connection of the square to the social building appears abrupt and not very precise
The high proportion of glass has a negative impact on costs
The building expression in the existing context and the dialogue between old and new are not entirely convincing
